newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian prosecutor raps U.S. at drug meeting.
newsitem.headline: Colombian prosecutor raps U.S. at drug meeting.

text.p: Colombia's chief prosecutor on Thursday criticised the United States for failing to attend an international meeting of counternarcotics experts in this Caribbean port city.
"This is very serious. I censure this action by the United States from every point of view," Prosecutor-General Alfonso Valdivieso told reporters.
He said the U.S. boycott of the meeting was inconsistent with Washington's claim that it is interested in doing everything possible to stem the flow of illegal narcotics into the United States.
As host, Colombia deserved an explanation of why the United States failed to attend, he added, saying participants from all 13 countries attending felt "snubbed" by Washington.

Valdivieso, Colombia's most popular and respected public official, is an anti-drug crusader who has been singled out for frequent praise by Washington. He is expected to step down soon to launch a campaign for the presidency in next year's elections.
Countries represented at the meeting, organised by Colombia's Foreign Ministry, include Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Portugal, Spain and a host of Latin American countries including Cuba.
The United States "decertified" Colombia in February for its alleged failures in the drug war.
